title: Voynich Paleography
summary: Davis explains how to apply Latin paleographic methods to the manuscript's recurring glyph shapes, stroke construction and spacing. The conference paper relates scribal attributions to codicology and proposes possible expansions of complex glyphs.
established: The analysis distinguishes five hands using shape and stroke differences in EVA k and n and cross-checks them with f. The long, low n flourishes on f66r prompted a reassignment from hand 3 to hand 5.
Differences in n flourish direction, extent and endpoint complement k crossbar construction and loop shape. Assignments rely on recurring combinations of features observed in image annotations.

open.question: Do the proposed component sequences for rare bridge-gallows give a consistent account of independently transcribed examples across writing contexts?
open.check: Freeze Davis's candidate decomposition rules, then compare the predicted component shapes and placements with blinded annotations of further bridge-gallows images.
